title: Forge Product Manifest
description: One declarative file per product (forge.yaml). The only artifact a human edits during routine onboarding. Rich enough to drive a build, a proposal, and a price. Contains NO secret values — credentials are referenced by name and resolved from a secrets provider at apply time.

catalog.description: The immutable catalog snapshot this product is pinned to. Pinning rather than floating is what makes a build reproducible eight months later.

snapshot.description: A dated snapshot id, or 'latest' which is refused by validate unless --allow-unpinned is passed.

id.description: Stable slug. Used in resource names, database names, and state paths, so it may never change after the first apply.

name.description: Human product name, shown in the application shell.

client.description: Used in proposals and generated documents.

legal_entity.description: Legal entity name. Invoice numbering is gapless and sequential per legal entity, so pay.invoices reads this.

vertical.description: Vertical template this product was initialised from. Informational in Phase 1; drives capability preselection from Phase 6.

branding.description: Branding a client is a kernel.ui token change and nothing else. Capabilities never ship their own styles.

tokens.description: Overrides for the kernel.ui token set. Unspecified tokens keep their default.

light.description: Repository-relative path to the light-theme logo.

capabilities.description: Selected capabilities. The kernel is mandatory and implicit — it is never listed here. Hard dependencies resolve automatically and the plan shows each addition and its price, so nothing is a surprise commercially or technically.

id.description: Must exist in the pinned catalog snapshot, and must not be a kernel capability.

version.description: Optional version range, narrowing what the snapshot offers. Omit in the normal case and let the snapshot decide.

config.description: Validated against this capability's declared config schema at validate time.

slots.description: Map of slot name to the repository-relative implementation path. Forge seeds a stub on first apply and never touches the file again.

enabled.description: false: retained in the manifest for documentation but excluded from the graph. Disabling a capability with applied migrations produces a destructive plan.

entities.description: Client-specific domain entities, declared here rather than invented in code. Because they are declared, they participate in permissions, audit, search, admin, and reporting automatically.

name.description: PascalCase. Must not collide with any entity owned by a capability in the resolved graph.

plural.description: Overrides naive pluralisation in admin and navigation labels.

personal_data.description: When data.privacy is enabled, an entity with this flag must declare a deletion strategy.

searchable.description: Indexed by data.search when present. Ignored with a warning when data.search is not in the graph.

type.description: A scalar type, a reference to another entity, or an enum.

default.description: Literal default value. Must type-check against `type`.

enum.description: Restricts a 'string' field to a closed set. Rendered as a select in admin and forms.

integrations.description: Configuration for the third-party services declared by selected capabilities. Every value that is a credential is a secret_ref — a NAME, never a value. Validate checks presence and readability only; apply resolves values in memory and never writes them to state, to a generated file, or to a log.

provider.description: Which provider satisfies this integration when a capability supports more than one.

credentials.description: Map of the credential name declared by the capability to a secret reference.

settings.description: Non-secret integration settings, e.g. a sending domain or a sandbox flag.

environments.description: One entry per environment. Each becomes a workspace: '<product.id>/<environment>'. Values here override the top-level defaults for that environment.

provider.description: local: codegen only, Docker Postgres, no cloud resources. gcp: Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, Cloud DNS (Phase 4).

project_id.description: GCP project. Required when provider is 'gcp'.

secrets.description: Where secret_ref names resolve for this environment.

path.description: For the 'file' provider. Must be gitignored; forge init generates the entry.

prefix.description: Namespace prepended to every secret_ref name.

capability_overrides.description: Per-environment config overrides, keyed by capability id. Use sparingly — divergence between staging and production is how surprises reach a client.

repository.description: Where the generated client application lives.

upgrade_strategy.description: How `forge fleet apply` lands changes. Pull requests are the default so a fleet upgrade is reviewable per client.

commercial.description: Inputs to `forge quote`. The engagement price is computed from the resolved graph — capability list prices plus a counted integration premium — not typed in here.

integration_rate_minor.description: Price per unit of computed integration weight, in minor units.

discount_minor.description: Absolute adjustment in minor units. Negative is a discount.

notes.description: Free text carried into the generated proposal.

secretRef.description: A NAME resolved from the environment's secrets provider at apply time. The manifest is committed and may be shared with a client, so it holds no values. Validate calls exists() and never reads the value; apply resolves in memory and never persists it to state, to a generated file, or to a log.
